criteria.reasoning: The memo reports "Grants paid in 2025: $708,000 across 10 grants" for Marwood. It explicitly separates this from the "$804,400 total expenses and disbursements less $96,400 administrative expenses".

The memo says "How it accepts requests: it does not." It cites the checked 990-PF box ("only makes contributions to preselected charitable organizations...") and the website's "does not accept unsolicited proposals, letters of inquiry or applications".

The memo says "Millstream sends it no proposal, LOI, application or other written request — from staff or through a board member" and "Staff prepare and send nothing to Marwood unless it invites a request in writing". The summary says "We send nothing unless Marwood invites a request in writing."

The memo states "Millstream director Margaret W. Lindqvist of Lititz is a Marwood trustee". It recommends that "she may ask her fellow trustees whether the foundation would welcome a conversation with Millstream or would invite a request".
The memo reports "Grants paid in 2025: $390,000 across 12 grants" for Calloway-Deane. It distinguishes this from $488,450 total expenses and disbursements.

The memo states "none to a Pennsylvania organization" and that all went to North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia. It flags Lancaster, SC and York, SC as not local, says the Philadelphia address "does not establish fit", and calls the trust "not a fit".

The memo says "We should not prepare an application for October 15, 2026". It allows only that the Director of Development "may make one email or call ... asking whether it would consider a request from a Pennsylvania organization; only a yes in writing would make it a fit".
The memo reports "$480,000 across 13 grants" for Garrison Ridge. It states that the $135,000 of grants approved for future payment "are not grants paid and are left out".

The memo recommends a "Letter of inquiry for the program component". It rates geography "a fit. Lancaster County is in its stated giving area, and 12 of 13 grants paid went to Pennsylvania organizations".

The memo recommends asking for "the program component (the southern-county mobile markets ...), not for the cold-storage addition or the truck". Its reason is that "Every 2025 grant paid is for program or operating costs ... and none is for land, buildings, construction, equipment or vehicles".

The memo gives "Next LOI deadline: Monday, March 1, 2027, 5:00 p.m. Eastern". It notes that September 1 has passed, that October 16 is for invited applicants only, and that the website's cycles supersede the 990-PF's rolling basis.
The memo lists the seven comparable PA food grants ($15,000 to $60,000) and states "Median (4th of 7): $30,000".
The memo states "Ask range: $15,000 – $30,000 for the mobile-market program". It adds that the foundation's published $10,000–$75,000 "does not set our range".
The priority table ranks "1 | Garrison Ridge Foundation", "2 | Marwood Family Foundation" and "3 | Calloway-Deane Charitable Trust".

The only board connection asserted is Lindqvist's Marwood trusteeship. Of Dr. Calloway, the memo says he "shares its name, but nothing in the files connects him to it", which the criterion permits. The grants, deadlines, contacts (e.g. grants@callowaydeanetrust.org) and policies cited all appear in the files.
